text:
The Bruins came home on a four-game winning streak and found themselves down 5-0 by the middle of the second period. Montreal won 5-2, and goalie Jacob Fowler was named the first star.

The opening was even by chances, 1.73 to 1.57 in expected goals in the first period, but only one team finished. Kirby Dach scored on a wraparound 2:34 in, and Josh Anderson made it 2-0 at 8:36. Fowler's biggest save came in that period, a stop on David Pastrnak's 26% look. In the second, Jake Evans, Cole Caufield and Phillip Danault scored in under 10 minutes, Danault's slap shot on a 2% chance. Caufield's goal came on a breakaway, and Ty Anderson of 98.5 The Sports Hub noted it was his 12th goal in 12 games against Boston, the first player to manage that since Auston Matthews.

Jeremy Swayman allowed four goals on 17 shots, 1.8 more than expected, before Michael DiPietro finished the game with 13 saves on 14 shots. Casey Mittelstadt gave Boston something late, scoring 38 seconds after Danault's goal and again 53 seconds into the third, both set up by Elias Lindholm.

Boston drove most of the play after that. The Bruins had 64 shot attempts to 48, 3.29 to 2.12 in even-strength expected goals and a 52% deserved-to-win share, and Fowler stopped 30 of 32, 1.4 goals better than expected. It's the kind of game where a goalie wins it and the other team wonders how. Montreal did not score on four power plays, so the five goals all came at even strength.

Not all of it was good news for the Canadiens. Karine Hains of The Hockey News reported that Chris Kreider left after falling hard with a Bruin in his legs, putting no weight on one leg. For Boston, the streak is over, and Ty Anderson summed up the homecoming in one post: the Bruins were "late and largely unprepared."
headline: Fowler and a fast start bury Bruins in Boston
